method_card.title: Family Members and Relationships
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family member vocabulary, possessive adjectives, and relationship status in German.

GermanEnglish
der Vaterfather
die Muttermother
der Bruderbrother
die Schwestersister
die Eltern (pl.)parents
die Geschwister (pl.)siblings
der Opa / die Omagrandpa / grandma
der Onkel / die Tanteuncle / aunt
der Stiefvaterstepfather
das Einzelkindonly child
verheiratetmarried
geschiedendivorced

Grammar focus: Possessive adjectives (mein, dein, sein, ihr) change their endings based on gender and case. Masculine nominative: mein Vater (no ending). Feminine/plural nominative: meine Mutter, meine Geschwister (add -e). Masculine accusative: meinen Vater (add -en).

Model: In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater, meine Mutter und meine Geschwister. Mein Bruder heißt Tom. Meine Eltern sind verheiratet. (In my family there is my father, my mother and my siblings. My brother is called Tom. My parents are married.)
steps: Learn family member nouns with their genders (der/die/das)
Master possessive adjective endings for nominative and accusative cases
Practice building sentences with 'In meiner Familie gibt es...'
Extend sentences with relative clauses (der/die/das + verb at end)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — family appears across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Meine Schwester heißt Anna und sie ist sehr lieb.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence at the conjunction und: 'Meine Schwester heißt Anna' + 'sie ist sehr lieb'.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Meine Schwester = my sister. heißt = is called. Anna = Anna.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: sie ist = she is. sehr = very. lieb = kind/sweet.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My sister is called Anna and she is very kind.

worked_examples.question: Why does 'meinen' have an -en ending in 'In meiner Familie gibt es meinen Vater'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Gibt es (there is/are) takes the accusative case because the family members are the direct object.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Vater is masculine (der Vater). In the accusative case, masculine possessive adjectives add -en.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Mein becomes meinen because Vater is masculine and follows gibt es (accusative). Feminine and neuter do not change: meine Mutter, mein Kind.

method_card.title: Personality and Character
method_card.content:
This lesson covers personality adjectives, intensifiers, relative clauses, and comparative forms for describing people.

GermanEnglish
freundlichfriendly
liebkind/sweet
ehrlichhonest
geduldigpatient
hilfsbereithelpful
witzigfunny
gemeinmean
faullazy
strengstrict
frechcheeky
ungeduldigimpatient
eifersüchtigjealous

Grammar focus: Relative clauses use der (masc.), die (fem./pl.) or das (neut.) and send the verb to the end. Comparatives add -er + als (than). Monosyllabic adjectives often gain an umlaut: alt → älter.

Model: Mein Vater, der sehr geduldig ist, hilft mir mit den Hausaufgaben. Meine Mutter ist geduldiger als mein Vater.
steps: Learn personality adjectives in positive-negative pairs
Use intensifiers (sehr, ziemlich, ein bisschen) to add detail
Build relative clauses with der/die/das + verb at end
Form comparatives with -er + als for comparing people

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — personality descriptions appear in every exam series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Mein Bruder ist ziemlich witzig, aber manchmal ein bisschen frech.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Split at aber (but): 'Mein Bruder ist ziemlich witzig' + 'manchmal ein bisschen frech'.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Mein Bruder = my brother. ist = is. ziemlich = quite. witzig = funny.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: manchmal = sometimes. ein bisschen = a bit. frech = cheeky.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My brother is quite funny, but sometimes a bit cheeky.

worked_examples.question: How do you form a relative clause in German to say 'My father, who is very patient, helps me'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Identify the noun: Mein Vater — masculine, so the relative pronoun is der.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Place a comma, then der, then the extra information, with the verb at the end: der sehr geduldig ist.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Close with another comma and continue the main clause. The main verb hilft comes next.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Mein Vater, der sehr geduldig ist, hilft mir.

method_card.title: Physical Appearance
method_card.content:
This lesson covers describing physical appearance using sein + adjective and haben + noun phrase, adjective agreement, and the separable verb aussehen.

GermanEnglish
blonde Haareblonde hair
braune Augenbrown eyes
kurze Haareshort hair
lange Haarelong hair
großtall
kleinshort
schlankslim
eine Brille tragento wear glasses
einen Barta beard
hübschpretty
sportlichsporty/athletic
aussehento look/appear

Grammar focus: Pattern 1: Er ist groß (sein + adjective, no ending change). Pattern 2: Er hat kurze Haare (haben + adjective before noun, ending must agree). Plural adjectives without article take -e. Masculine accusative after einen takes -en.

Model: Er ist groß und schlank. Er hat kurze schwarze Haare und blaue Augen. Er sieht sportlich aus.
steps: Learn hair and eye colour vocabulary with correct adjective endings
Use 'sein + adjective' for general descriptions and 'haben + noun' for specific features
Master adjective endings: -e for plural, -en after einen (masculine accusative)
Practice the separable verb aussehen for photo descriptions

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — photo descriptions in speaking exam

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Sie hat lange blonde Haare und grüne Augen.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Sie hat = She has. lange = long. blonde = blonde. Haare = hair.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: und = and. grüne = green. Augen = eyes.

steps.label: Answer

worked_examples.question: Why does the adjective ending change in 'Er hat einen schwarzen Bart' but not in 'Er ist groß'?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: In Er ist groß, the adjective comes after the verb sein. Adjectives after verbs do not change their ending.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: In Er hat einen schwarzen Bart, the adjective schwarz comes before the noun Bart. Before a noun, adjectives must agree in gender and case.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Bart is masculine and follows einen (accusative). After einen, the adjective takes -en: einen schwarzen Bart.

obwohlalthough (verb to end)

Grammar focus: Weil and obwohl are subordinating conjunctions — the verb goes to the end. Denn is coordinating — normal word order. Trotzdem is an adverb — verb comes immediately after it.

Model: Mein bester Freund heißt Max. Er ist mein bester Freund, weil er immer für mich da ist. Trotzdem ist er manchmal ein bisschen faul.
steps: Learn friendship vocabulary in positive-negative pairs
Master weil and obwohl — verb goes to the END of the clause

Include trotzdem to show contrast and grammatical range

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: With weil: Join them: Er ist ein guter Freund, weil er geduldig ist.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: After weil, the conjugated verb moves to the end of the clause. Always place a comma before weil.

worked_examples.question: What is the difference between 'weil' and 'denn'?

steps.label: Step 2

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Denn (coordinating): normal word order. Er ist gut, denn er ist ehrlich.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Using both weil and denn in the same piece of writing shows the examiner you understand the difference — this earns higher marks for grammatical range.

method_card.title: Relationships, Marriage and Future Plans
method_card.content:
This lesson covers relationships, marriage pros and cons, and the conditional tense for future plans.

GermanEnglish
die Hochzeitthe wedding
die Ehemarriage
heiratento get married
zusammenwohnento live together
ich möchteI would like
ich würdeI would
hättewould have
wärewould be
ledig bleibento stay single
einerseits / andererseitson one hand / on the other hand

Grammar focus: Conditional tense: möchte/würde + infinitive at end. Hätte (would have) and wäre (would be) are standalone. The conditional counts as a separate time frame for AO3 marks.

Model: Ich möchte in zehn Jahren heiraten. Mein idealer Partner wäre geduldig und hätte braune Haare. Einerseits ist die Ehe romantisch, andererseits kostet es zu viel.
steps: Learn marriage and relationship vocabulary (Hochzeit, Ehe, heiraten)
Master the conditional tense: möchte/würde + infinitive at end
Use hätte (would have) and wäre (would be) for ideal partner descriptions
Present balanced arguments using einerseits/andererseits

exam_context.frequency: Higher tier topic — conditional tense essential for Grade 5+

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Ich möchte in zehn Jahren heiraten.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Ich möchte = I would like. This is the conditional verb.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: in zehn Jahren = in ten years. This is the time phrase.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: heiraten = to get married. This is the infinitive at the end.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I would like to get married in ten years.

worked_examples.question: Explain the word order rule with 'möchte' and 'würde'.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Möchte and würde are conditional verbs. They go in position 2 (conjugated).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The main verb (infinitive) goes to the end of the sentence.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Pattern: Subject + möchte/würde + extra info + infinitive. Example: Ich möchte ein Haus kaufen.

method_card.title: Food and Drink
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, expressing preferences with adverbs of manner, and ordering food politely.

GermanEnglish
das Brotbread
das Fleischmeat
der Fischfish
das Obstfruit
das Gemüsevegetables
die Pommeschips/fries
das Wasserwater
der Kaffeecoffee
gernlike (doing)
lieberprefer (doing)
am liebstenlike most (doing)
ich möchte / ich hätte gernI would like

Grammar focus: Adverbs of manner (gern, nicht gern, lieber, am liebsten) come after the verb: Ich esse gern Obst. The strong verb essen changes stem: du isst, er/sie isst. Use zum + meal for 'for breakfast/lunch/dinner'.

Model: Ich esse gern Obst, weil es gesund ist. Am liebsten esse ich Hähnchen. Zum Frühstück trinke ich Orangensaft.
steps: Learn food and drink nouns with their genders (der/die/das)
Use gern/nicht gern/lieber/am liebsten AFTER the verb

method_card.title: Health, Fitness and Lifestyle
method_card.content:
This lesson covers healthy lifestyle activities, body parts, talking about illness, modal verbs for health advice, and the perfect tense with haben and sein.

GermanEnglish
schwimmento swim
laufento run
Fahrrad fahrento ride a bike
Sport treibento do sport
der Kopfhead
Kopfschmerzenheadache
Bauchschmerzenstomach ache
man mussyou must
man sollyou should
man darf nichtyou must not

Grammar focus: Modal verbs (muss, soll, darf, kann) send the infinitive to the end. Perfect tense: haben for most verbs, sein for movement verbs (gelaufen, geschwommen, gegangen). Compound nouns: body part + Schmerzen.

Model: Man muss Sport treiben, um fit zu bleiben. Ich bin im Park gelaufen. Ich habe Kopfschmerzen.
steps: Learn body parts and form compound nouns with Schmerzen
Use modal verbs (muss/soll/darf) with infinitive at the END
Choose haben or sein for perfect tense: sein for movement verbs
Use um...zu (in order to) to explain health habits

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Use haben for everything else: eating, drinking, playing, reading, sleeping.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: The main verb goes to the end as an infinitive.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Man muss Obst essen. (You must eat fruit.) Man darf nicht rauchen. (You must not smoke.)

method_card.title: School Life, Rules and Uniform
method_card.content:
This lesson covers school facilities, school rules with modal verbs, school uniform with accusative adjective endings, and dass opinion clauses.

GermanEnglish
das Klassenzimmerclassroom
die Kantinecanteen
die Bibliotheklibrary
die Turnhallegymnasium
man mussyou must
man darf nichtyou must not
die Schuluniformschool uniform
einen roten Rocka red skirt
eine blaue Hoseblue trousers
ein weißes Hemda white shirt
tragento wear
Ich denke, dass...I think that...

Grammar focus: Modal verbs for rules: man muss/soll/darf (nicht) + infinitive at end. Clothing with accusative adjective endings: -en (masc.), -e (fem.), -es (neut.), -e (pl.). Dass clauses send the verb to the end.

Model: In meiner Schule gibt es eine Kantine. Man muss die Schuluniform tragen. Ich trage einen roten Rock und ein weißes Hemd. Ich denke, dass die Uniform praktisch ist.
steps: Learn school facility vocabulary with es gibt
Express rules using man muss/soll/darf (nicht) + infinitive at end
Describe uniform with accusative adjective endings (-en, -e, -es)
Give opinions with Ich denke/finde/glaube, dass... (verb at end)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — school life in 50-word writing task

worked_examples.question: How do you describe school uniform using accusative adjective endings?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Use tragen (to wear). It takes the accusative case.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Masculine: einen roten Rock. Feminine: eine blaue Hose. Neuter: ein weißes Hemd. Plural: schwarze Schuhe.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich trage einen roten Rock, eine blaue Hose, ein weißes Hemd und schwarze Schuhe.

worked_examples.question: How do dass clauses work?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Dass (that) is a subordinating conjunction. Like weil and obwohl, it sends the verb to the end.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Opinion verbs: Ich denke (I think), Ich finde (I find), Ich glaube (I believe).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich denke, dass die Schuluniform wichtig ist. (I think that school uniform is important.)
